exposure: gestational age at birth (34, 35, and 36 weeks)
outcome: temperature at birth and two hours after admission
cohort: 276 late preterm infants (born at 34 to 36 weeks of gestation) at a single center
finding: Late preterm infants, especially at 34 weeks, are at higher risk for complications during the transition to extrauterine life, including resuscitation, hypothermia, and respiratory problems.
